clue.text: Jumper might go over this, missing tie

parts.note: skipping a class means missing it
to rope something is to tie it up

explanation.surface: Something a sweater passes over, minus a necktie: a wardrobe scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' reads as a sweater, as in British English, but here it is a person who jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A child skipping swings a cord under their feet and hops over it each turn.

clue.text: Relegated team getting stuffed

parts.note: a side is a sports team
lined, as a purse lined with money is stuffed

explanation.surface: A football team goes down a division and gets thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffed' sounds like a heavy defeat, but it means filled, so LINED.
explanation.definitionFit: A player relegated to a minor role is pushed out of the action, kept on the bench.

clue.text: One piece of turf outside recently cut off

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the turf word sits around the word for recently, enclosing it

parts.note: a sod is a clod of turf
late, as in 'of late', means recently

explanation.surface: A single clod of grass lies outside, newly dug up.
explanation.definitionFit: A village cut off by floods is isolated, separated from everywhere else.

clue.text: Bit of pastry on outside of cake

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word cake, its first and last

explanation.surface: A baker puts pastry on the outer layer of a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit and a piece are both synonyms for a small portion of something.

clue.text: Forget it? Number always on memory

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
to keep something in mind is to hold it in memory

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a number is permanently lodged in memory or lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom telling someone to drop the matter, the same as saying forget it.

clue.text: Object to nurse cutting break

indicators.note: the nurse abbreviation cuts into the break word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a rest is a break
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse objects to having her break cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To object to something is to take offence at it, a synonym of feeling bitter about it.

clue.text: European side left with no goals

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a score of nil, nought, is the letter O

explanation.surface: A European football team plays on the left and scores nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: FC Porto is a leading Portuguese football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The football club FC Porto is a Portuguese team, so a side from Europe.

clue.text: Out-of-shape group of patients receiving exercise classes

indicators.note: the ward takes in the exercise abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: a hospital ward holds a group of patients
PE is physical education, school exercise classes

explanation.surface: Unfit hospital patients are given exercise sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something warped is twisted or bent, no longer keeping its true form.

clue.text: Cleaner bum

definitions.meaning: a soft absorbent pad used for washing
to scrounge or cadge off others, as a freeloader does

explanation.definitionFit: A bath pad for washing, and a verb for living off others: to cadge, as a freeloader does.

clue.text: See 22
Pulls out of hospital procedure after doctor gives you bug

indicators.note: the procedure word comes after the doctor abbreviation
the hospital letter is taken out of the word for pulls

parts.note: heaves means pulls hard
an op is a surgical procedure

explanation.surface: A patient discharges themselves after an operation, and the doctor passes on an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes H from HEAVES, leaving EAVES. 'Bug' looks like a germ but is a verb: to listen in.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug a room is to listen in secretly on what is said there.

clue.text: Time for contraception? Strip

parts.note: the Pill is an oral contraceptive
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A question about when to take contraception, then a terse command to undress.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip a town of valuables is to plunder or loot it.

clue.text: Weary race to the bottom?

parts.note: a run is a race
down means towards the bottom

explanation.surface: A tired person thinks of a race to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling run-down means being tired and in poor health, so exhausted.

clue.text: Perhaps rock and roll CD in US came out

indicators.note: out, as in a bone put out, suggests the letters dislocated into a new order

explanation.surface: A rock and roll album was released in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CD IN US CAME; 'came' is fodder, not part of the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock and roll is an example of music for dancing to, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Supporting being raised on farm

parts.note: up means raised
a holding is a piece of farmland

explanation.surface: Someone backs a child brought up on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Upholding a decision means backing or supporting it.

clue.text: See 22
Help to smuggle cocaine: tips for drug users

indicators.note: smuggling hides something within, so the cocaine letter goes inside the help word

parts.note: aid means help
C is slang shorthand for cocaine
heads are the tips or tops of things

explanation.surface: Advice on helping to smuggle drugs, written for users.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is slang for LSD, and its regular takers are heavy users of that drug.

clue.text: Balloon with delivery following small present

indicators.note: following sends the delivery word after the small and present pieces

parts.note: now means at present
a ball is a delivery from a cricket bowler

explanation.surface: A balloon comes with the post, after a little gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' is a bowled ball in cricket, placed by 'following' after S and NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: When costs balloon they grow rapidly, as a rolling mass gathers size.

clue.text: Sit on river and fish

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler sits by a river and fishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride a horse or bike is to sit astride it while it moves.

clue.text: Part of salad not left on a plate

parts.note: the opposite of left is right, R
a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: Some salad has been left on a plate, uneaten.
explanation.definitionFit: This red root vegetable is a common salad ingredient.

clue.text: Suspect shot: unwind seeing crime dramas

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A suspect is shot, then the viewer unwinds watching detective shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Detective stories that keep the culprit secret until the end are crime dramas.

clue.text: Relax with partner after endless sex

indicators.note: the partner word comes after the trimmed sex word
the word sex loses its final letter

parts.note: a date is a romantic partner

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds with a lover after a marathon session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops X from SEX, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sedate a patient is to calm them down with a drug.

clue.text: Pure soprano voices

parts.note: utter means pure or absolute, as in 'utter nonsense'

explanation.surface: A soprano sings with pure tones.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to say it, so voices is a verb meaning speaks out.

clue.text: Performing it, Dua Lipa got idea for recording

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters put on a show, worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Dua Lipa, while performing a song, had a brainstorm about how to record it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing' rearranges IT DUA LIPA GOT IDEA. Dua Lipa is a British pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: This cassette format stores sound as digital data, a medium for recording.

clue.text: Country harvest picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to garner is to harvest or gather in

explanation.surface: A country's crops are gathered in.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: This West African nation is a republic on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Around centre of town, spilled milk here?

parts.note: C is short for circa, around

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word town

parts.note: shed means spilled or poured out

explanation.surface: Someone asks if milk was spilled near the middle of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairy cows are housed and milked in a farm building, so this is where you would milk.

clue.text: One's rolled up with soldier upset in vehicle

indicators.note: the reversed soldier sits in the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier sits upset in a vehicle, rolling a smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' reads the soldier upwards; 'One's rolled up' is the definition, not more wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco leaves are rolled tightly to make this smoke.

clue.text: English call on John Barnes, ultimately to lead dribbling

indicators.note: the last letter of Barnes is placed at the front, leading the rest
on places the English and call pieces after the John word, following it
ultimately points to the final letter of Barnes

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is lav
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: An English commentator calls on footballer John Barnes to start a dribble.
explanation.walkthrough: John Barnes, an England winger famous for dribbling, misdirects: 'John' is the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavering means drooling, letting saliva run from the mouth.

clue.text: Group of drivers right to restrict parking out of consideration

indicators.note: restricting the parking letter means boxing it in, so it goes inside

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: Motorists' group claims a right to limit parking.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring breakdown service.
explanation.definitionFit: Joking apart, setting it apart: the word means aside, excluded from consideration.

clue.text: Serve sugarless cola without opening snacks

indicators.note: serve suggests letters dished up in a new arrangement
the word cola loses its first letter

explanation.surface: An order to serve diet cola with the cap still on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without opening' drops C from COLA, leaving OLA; 'Serve' rearranges SUGARLESS with OLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausage meat baked in pastry makes a popular British party snack.
